source.title: Understanding and Utilizing Deep Neural Networks Trained with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Pengfei Chen; B. Liao; Guang-Yong Chen; Sheng-Yu Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes and experimentally measures training and test behavior under synthetic label noise, including fully random labels; it is not an explicit replication of the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) and Arpit et al. (2017), but those cited findings are not rows. Its own experiments report training accuracy at several noise ratios and compare test accuracy with theoretical estimates. Figure 2 values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study measures fitting of corrupted labels by normally trained ResNet-110. Crucially, its symmetric-noise definition produces completely random labels at ε=0.9 for ten classes, not ε=1.0. Its low training accuracy at ε=0.9 bears directly on V1 and the regularization component of V5; the high-noise sweep also bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' stated conclusion but needs clarification: they argue that sufficiently rich networks trained to convergence reproduce the label-noise distribution, even when training accuracy is low. Their language about fitting the training set must not be read as empirical evidence of zero training error. They also conclude that INCV identifies clean samples and improves robust-training performance when combined with Co-teaching.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies synthetic label corruption with cross-validation and measures training and held-out behavior; it does not reproduce the original study's full experimental protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy at high symmetric noise is affected by the use of standard data augmentation, as discussed by the authors.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out noisy-label accuracy follows a noise-dependent quadratic under symmetric corruption and a different quadratic under asymmetric corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models' agreement with independently corrupted held-out labels can be characterized using the label-noise transition matrix.

record.problems: The reported high-noise training accuracies are aggregate values without uncertainty in the main text; plotted test-accuracy values are figure-only here. The authors state that standard data augmentation makes high training accuracy difficult to achieve.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 also plots label precision and label recall, which do not measure the behaviors named by the claim versions. Figure 3 and Supplementary Figure 7 show confusion matrices and are not separately extracted because they measure prediction distributions rather than the versions' specified outcomes.

untested.parts: No explicit numerical clean-test chance result accompanies the random-label training accuracy. Supplement A.1 specifies a common architecture and training schedule, but there is no demonstrated successful interpolation of random labels under that schedule.
No comparison of time to fit true versus random labels or convergence time across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-input experiments.
No extracted clean-label test-error sweep establishes steady degradation while retaining perfect training fit; remaining-signal learning and noise memorization are not separately measured.

No dropout experiment, separate regularizer ablations, or experiment removing regularization and measuring true-label generalization. The assertion about fitting without augmentation relies on cited expressiveness results.
No direct trajectories comparing acquisition of shared real patterns with memorization of corrupted labels. Clean-test trajectories for noise-mitigation methods do not establish that ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Definition 1 gives Tii=1−ε and Tij=ε/9, so complete label independence occurs at ε=0.9. At ε=1.0, labels retain an exclusion relationship with the true class. Confusion-matrix results are already declared in rows_left_out; mitigation-method comparisons and sample-selection scores do not establish the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests symmetric noise through ratio 1.0, but does not report a separate test-error-at-chance result for fully random labels or compare unchanged hyperparameters against another training setup.

The study tests symmetric noise ratios up to 1.0 and reports low training accuracy at high noise. It does not test a steadily rising test error while training remains perfectly fit, or isolate capture of remaining signal from memorization.

rows.subject: ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with symmetric label noise; training accuracy reported after convergence.
rows.note: The reported accuracy is far from perfect fitting; the authors attribute difficulty achieving high training accuracy to data augmentation.
rows.check: The 0.58 training accuracy is correct, but ε=0.7 retains label signal and does not test V1's completely random labeling. Add the Supplement A.1 conditions: Adam, 200 epochs, weight decay 10^-4, random cropping and horizontal flipping; training uses half of CIFAR-10.

rows.subject: ResNet-110

rows.subject: ResNet-110
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy over symmetric and asymmetric noise-ratio sweeps using cross-validation.

conditions.value: sweep; individual plotted values not transcribed

rows.measure: test accuracy on held-out noisy split
rows.note: The authors state that experimental results are consistent with theoretical estimates and that test accuracy depends on noise ratio; the figure does not establish the V4 condition of perfect training fit.
rows.check: This measures agreement with corrupted held-out labels, rather than V4's generalization to true labels. It also combines symmetric and asymmetric corruption and supplies no readable experimental values. The stated dependence on noise ratio cannot establish V4's steadily worsening clean-label test error.

tranche.reason: The study investigates fitting and generalization under synthetic label corruption using cross-validation and a different training protocol.

source_check.notes: Section 5.1 evaluates held-out data sharing the training noise, so its test-accuracy curve is not clean-test accuracy. The four training accuracies have no stated uncertainty or separate unaugmented training-set evaluation.

statements.correction: ResNet-110: 200 epochs using Adam; initial learning rate 10^-3; learning rate divided by 10 after epochs 80, 120 and 160, then by 2 after epoch 180; batch size 128.
statements.problem: The assertion that the ResNet training budget is not supplied contradicts Supplement A.1.
